title: Configuring the DLP Application Integration Using Google Cloud Platform

blocks.text: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) only supports the Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding method for DLP application integration in Workflow Automation.

You must integrate Workflow Automation with the GCP using Zscaler Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding to allow the Zscaler service to send Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy violations to GCP cloud storage. Configuring GCP with Zscaler incident forwarding enables your organization to send DLP incident metadata and evidence files to your organization's GCP storage buckets without deploying appliances.

You can also configure the DLP application integration using Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure. To learn more, see Configuring the DLP Application Integration Using Amazon Web Services and Configuring the DLP Application Integration Using Azure.

To view the various IP addresses of different Workflow Automation clouds associated with Zscaler, see NAT Gateway IP addresses. Ensure that these NAT Gateway IPs are allowed on the storage account. You can find your cloud in the URL that admins use to log in to the Zscaler Admin Console. For example, if you log in to https://app.us1.zsworkflow.net/, then your organization's cloud is produs1.
To configure the DLP application integration using Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding:

blocks.item: 1. Create cloud resources in GCP.

You can create cloud resources by creating a GCP integration cloud resource stack in GCP, or you can create them manually using the Google Cloud console or the Google Cloud command line interface (CLI).

Google is discontinuing support for the Google Cloud Deployment Manager on March 31, 2026. After that date, create the resources manually. Zscaler is in the process of defining a replacement process. To learn more, see Cloud Deployment Manager deprecation.
Creating Cloud Resources Using a DLP GCP Integration Cloud Resource Stack in GCP
a. Download the Zscaler script from the Zscaler Admin Console.
To download Zscaler deployment script:

From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Workflow Automation > Integrations. The Integrations dashboard appears, displaying a DLP GCP application tile. The Tile View icon is selected by default.
See image.
Click anywhere within the DLP GCP application tile. The Zscaler DLP GCP Integration details page appears, displaying a Configuration Steps tab and a Configuration tab.
See image.
Click the Configuration Steps tab. Under GCP Cloud Resource Stack Setup, click the deployment.jinja link to download the DLP GCP Integration cloud resource stack.
See image.
b. Create cloud resources for the DLP integration.
To create cloud resources:
Log in to the Google Admin Console.
Using the Project Selection drop-down menu, select your organization.
In the resource table that appears, select the appropriate domain.
See image.
In the top right of the Google Cloud console, click the Activate Cloud Shell icon. The Cloud Shell virtual terminal appears at the bottom of the page.
See image.
In the Cloud Shell prompt, run the following command:
nano deployment.jinja
Copy and paste the content from the deployment.jinja file you downloaded earlier into the Cloud Shell prompt.
See image.
Check the deployment storage account permissions. You need editor, resource manager, and pubsub admin permissions for the storage accounts used for the deployment:
To get the project number, run the following command:
gcloud projects describe <PROJECT_ID> --format="value(projectNumber)"
You are assigned a project number that you can use for the next steps.
To check whether you have the required permissions, run the following command:

gcloud projects get-iam-policy <PROJECT_ID> --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings.members:'serviceAccount:<PROJECT_NUMBER>@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com'" --format='table(bindings.role)'
The following image is an example of the command's output:
See image.
If you do not have the required permissions for the storage accounts, run the following commands:
To provide resource manager permission:
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <PROJECT_ID> --member="serviceAccount:<PROJECT_NUMBER>@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin"
To provide pubsub admin permission:
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <PROJECT_ID> --member="serviceAccount:<PROJECT_NUMBER>@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/pubsub.admin"
By default, you have editor permissions for the storage accounts.
Create a deployment for the cloud resources:
To create storage buckets with default Google-managed encryption keys, run the following command:
gcloud deployment-manager deployments create <DEPLOYMENT_NAME> --template=<TEMPLATE_NAME> --properties="prefix:<PREFIX>,location:<LOCATION>
To create storage buckets with customer-managed KMS keys, run the following command:
gcloud deployment-manager deployments create <DEPLOYMENT_NAME> --template=<TEMPLATE_NAME> --properties="prefix:<PREFIX>,location:<LOCATION>,kms_key:<KMS_KEY>
The kms_key should follow the format: projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/keyRings/my-key-ring/cryptoKeys/my-key.
Ensure that you replace the following fields in red with the appropriate values:
<PROJECT_ID>: The organization's project ID.
<PROJECT_NUMBER>: The project number of the deployment.
<DEPLOYMENT_NAME>: The name of the cloud resource deployment.
<TEMPLATE_NAME>: The name of the deployment script template.
<PREFIX>: A unique prefix to identify the cloud resources being created. Add this value before topic, data, and metadata buckets. You cannot use dots (.) in the prefix.
<LOCATION>: The geographical location where the cloud resources are deployed (e.g., us-central1).
<KMS_KEY>: (Optional) The full resource name of the cloud KMS key. The buckets are encrypted by default and managed by Google.
If you have access to your own KMS key, run the following command before creating the cloud resource deployment. If you don't run this command, the deployment fails.
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding <KEY_NAME> --location <LOCATION> --keyring --member "serviceAccount:<PROJECT_NUMBER>@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com"
The following is an example command:
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding zwa-key --location us-central1 --keyring zwa-key-ring --member "serviceAccount:23456710100@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com".
<KEY_NAME>: The name of the KMS key.
<KEYRING_NAME>: The name of the key ring.
Optionally, you can include the retention period (days) for the data and metadata buckets in the deployment command to manage their lifecycle. The following is an example command:

gcloud deployment-manager deployments create zwa --template=deployment.jinja --properties="prefix:zwa,location:us-central1,kms_key:projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/keyRings/my-key-ring/cryptoKeys/my-key, retention_period_data:30,retention_period_metadata:30"
See image.
After completing the deployment, Google Cloud console creates the storage accounts and storage buckets based on your input values.
c. Create the service account private key.
To create a private key:
In the Google Cloud console, go to IAM & Admin > Service Accounts. The Service accounts page appears.
On the Service accounts page, filter to find the newly created service account and select it. The service account details page appears.
See image.
On the service account details page, click the Keys tab.
On the Keys tab, from the Add key drop-down menu, select Create new key. The Create private key window appears.
See image.
In the Create private key window, select JSON as the Key type and click Create.
See image.

A file containing the service account key values is downloaded to your local system. These values are required when creating the DLP GCP Integration in the Zscaler Admin Console. The following image displays example key values.
See image.
Creating Cloud Resources Manually Using the Google Cloud Console or the Google Cloud CLI
You can manually create and configure GCP resources using the Google Cloud console or the Google Cloud CLI.

Make sure the following prerequisites are met. If you are going to use the Google Cloud console, make note of these environment values for reference. If you are going to run the Google Cloud commands, set the following environment variables in the shell.

# The prefix for all your resources. It cannot contain a period (.). export PREFIX="<PREFIX>" # The GCP location for your resources (e.g., us-central1). export LOCATION="<LOCATION>" # The GCP Project ID where resources will be created. export PROJECT_ID=$(gcloud config get-value project) # The Project Number for your GCP project. export PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format="value(projectNumber)") # (Optional) The retention period in days for the data bucket. # If not needed, leave it empty. Example: export RETENTION_PERIOD_DATA="<30>" export RETENTION_PERIOD_DATA="" # (Optional) The retention period in days for the metadata bucket. # If not needed, leave it empty. Example: export RETENTION_PERIOD_METADATA="<365>" export RETENTION_PERIOD_METADATA="" # (Optional) The full resource name of the KMS key for encryption. # If not needed, leave it empty. # Example: export KMS_KEY="<projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/keyRings/my-keyring/cryptoKeys/my-key>" export KMS_KEY="" # --- Derived Variables (no need to change these) --- export ZSCALER_SA="zscaler-sa-${PREFIX}@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com" export GCS_SA="service-${PROJECT_NUMBER}@gs-project-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com" export DATA_BUCKET_NAME="${PREFIX}-data" export METADATA_BUCKET_NAME="${PREFIX}-metadata" export PUBSUB_TOPIC_NAME="${PREFIX}-file-events-topic"
Ensure that you replace the following fields in red with the appropriate values:
<PREFIX>: The prefix for all of your organization's resources.
<LOCATION>: The geographical location where the cloud resources are deployed (e.g., us-central1).

blocks.heading: Manually Creating and Configuring GCP Resources

blocks.item: To manually create and configure GCP resources using the Google Cloud console or the Google Cloud CLI:
a. Create a Zscaler service account.
Create a dedicated service account for the Zscaler integration. Zscaler uses this service account to access the resources you create.
Using Google Cloud Console
In to the Google Cloud console, go to IAM & Admin > Service Accounts. The Service accounts page appears, listing all the service accounts.
See image.
On the Service accounts page, click Create service account. The Create service account page appears.
On the Create service account page, in the Create service account section:
Service account name: Enter a name for the service account—for example, zscaler-sa-<PREFIX>.
Service account ID: The sytem automatically populates this field.
Service account description: Enter a description for the service account.
Skip granting project-level roles and access to the service account on this page. Later, in the Assign IAM Permissions step, you grant more specific permissions.
See image.
Click Create and continue.
Click Done. The newly created service account appears in the list of service accounts on the Service accounts page.
Using Google Cloud CLI
Enter the following command:
gcloud iam service-accounts create "zscaler-sa-${PREFIX}" \ --display-name="ZScaler Service Account - ${PREFIX}" \ --project="${PROJECT_ID}"
b. Create a data bucket.

Create the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket to store data files. The data bucket includes configurations for versioning, uniform access control, and optional retention policies and Key Management Service (KMS) encryption.
Using Google Cloud Console
In the Google Cloud console, go to Cloud Storage > Buckets. The Buckets page appears, listing all the buckets.
See image.
On the Buckets page, click Create. The Create a bucket page appears.
On the Create a bucket page, in the Get Started section, enter the name for the data bucket—for example, <PREFIX>-data.
Click Continue.
In the Choose where to store your data section, select the location and location type where you want to store the data.
Click Continue.
In the Choose how to store your data section, select the Standard option as the default storage class.
Click Continue.
In the Choose how to control access to objects section:
Public access prevention: By default, this checkbox is selected. Leave the default setting.
Access Control: Select the Uniform access control option.
See image.
Click Continue.
In the Choose how to protect object data section:
Protection tools: Select the Object versioning option.

Data Encryption: (Optional) If you are using a KMS key, select Customer-managed encryption key and enter your KMS key. This value corresponds to the KMS_KEY environment variable as indicated in the Prerequisites section.
Click Continue.
(Optional) Set a retention policy:
Expand the Lifecycle section.
Click Add a Rule.
Under Select an action, select Delete.

Under Select object conditions, select Age and enter the desired retention period in days. This value corresponds to the RETENTION_PERIOD_DATA environment variable as indicated in the Prerequisites section.
Click Save.
Click Create.
Using Google Cloud CLI
Enter the following commands:

# Create the bucket gcloud storage buckets create "gs://${DATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \ --location="${LOCATION}" \ --default-storage-class="STANDARD" \ --uniform-bucket-level-access # Enable versioning gcloud storage buckets update "gs://${DATA_BUCKET_NAME}" --versioning # (Optional) Set KMS encryption key if [[ -n "$KMS_KEY" ]]; then gcloud storage buckets update "gs://${DATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --default-kms-key="${KMS_KEY}" fi # (Optional) Set retention policy if [[ -n "$RETENTION_PERIOD_DATA" ]]; then RETENTION_SECONDS=$((RETENTION_PERIOD_DATA * 86400)) echo '{ "rule": [ { "action": {"type": "Delete"}, "condition": {"age": '"$RETENTION_PERIOD_DATA"'} } ] }' > /tmp/data-lifecycle.json gcloud storage buckets update "gs://${DATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --lifecycle-file=/tmp/data-lifecycle.json fi
c. Create a metadata bucket.
Create the GCS bucket to store the metadata. You can configure the metadata bucket with its own optional retention policy.
Using Google Cloud Console
In the Google Cloud console, go to Cloud Storage > Buckets. The Buckets page appears, listing all the buckets.
See image.
On the Buckets page, click Create. The Create a bucket page appears.
In the Get Started section, enter the name for the data bucket—for example, <PREFIX>-metadata.
Click Continue.
In the Choose where to store your data section, select the location and location type where you want to store the data.
Click Continue.
In the Choose how to store your data section, select the Standard option as the default storage class.
Click Continue.
In the Choose how to control access to objects section:
Public access prevention: By default, this checkbox is selected. Leave the default setting.
Access Control: Select the Uniform access control option.
See image.
Click Continue.
In the Choose how to protect object data section:
Protection tools: Select the Object versioning option.

Data Encryption: (Optional) If you are using a KMS key, select Customer-managed encryption key and enter your KMS key. This value corresponds to the KMS_KEY environment variable as indicated in the Prerequisites section.
Click Continue.
(Optional) Set a retention policy:
Expand the Lifecycle section.
Click Add a Rule.
Under Select an action, select Delete.

Under Select object conditions, select Age and enter the desired retention period in days. This value corresponds to the RETENTION_PERIOD_METADATA environment variable as indicated in the Prerequisites section.
Click Save.
Click Create.
Using Google Cloud CLI
Enter the following commands:

# Create the bucket gcloud storage buckets create "gs://${METADATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \ --location="${LOCATION}" \ --default-storage-class="STANDARD" \ --uniform-bucket-level-access # Enable versioning gcloud storage buckets update "gs://${METADATA_BUCKET_NAME}" --versioning # (Optional) Set KMS encryption key if [[ -n "$KMS_KEY" ]]; then gcloud storage buckets update "gs://${METADATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --default-kms-key="${KMS_KEY}" fi # (Optional) Set retention policy if [[ -n "$RETENTION_PERIOD_METADATA" ]]; then RETENTION_SECONDS=$((RETENTION_PERIOD_METADATA * 86400)) echo '{ "rule": [ { "action": {"type": "Delete"}, "condition": {"age": '"$RETENTION_PERIOD_METADATA"'} } ] }' > /tmp/data-lifecycle.json gcloud storage buckets update "gs://${METADATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --lifecycle-file=/tmp/data-lifecycle.json fi
d. Create a Pub/Sub topic and grant permissions.

Create a Pub/Sub topic for GCS notifications and grant the GCS service account permission to publish messages to it. This topic receives notifications when new objects are uploaded to the metadata bucket.
Using Google Cloud Console
In the Google Cloud console, go to Pub/Sub > Topics. The Topics page appears, listing all the topics.
See image.
On the Topics page, click Create topic. The Create topic page appears.
On the Create topic page, in the Topic ID field, enter <PREFIX>-file-events-topic.
Deselect Add a default subscription. By default, this checkbox is selected. Leave the other default settings.
See image.
Click Create.
Using Google Cloud CLI
Enter the following commands:

# Create the Pub/Sub topic gcloud pubsub topics create "${PUBSUB_TOPIC_NAME}" \ --project="${PROJECT_ID}" # Grant GCS service account publisher role on the topic gcloud pubsub topics add-iam-policy-binding "${PUBSUB_TOPIC_NAME}" \ --member="serviceAccount:${GCS_SA}" \ --role="roles/pubsub.publisher" \ --project="${PROJECT_ID}"
e. Create a notification for the metadata bucket.
Configure the metadata bucket to send a notification to the Pub/Sub topic whenever a new object is created.
Using Google Cloud Console
In the Google Cloud console, go to Cloud Storage > Buckets. The Buckets page appears, listing all the buckets.

On the Buckets page, in the list of buckets, click the name of your metadata bucket. This corresponds to the METADATA_BUCKET_NAME environment value as indicated in the Prerequisites section. The Bucket details page appears.
On the Bucket details page, click the Notifications tab. If this tab is not available, create the notification using the Google Cloud CLI.
Click Create Notification. A configuration pane appears on the right side of the page.
In the configuration pane:
From the Topic ID dropdown menu, select the Pub/Sub topic you want to send notifications to. This corresponds to the PUBSUB_TOPIC_NAME environment value as indicated in the Prerequisites section.
Under Select event types, select Object finalization. When a new object is created in the bucket, this event is triggered.
Leave the Payload format as JSON API v1, which appears by default.
Click Save.
Using Google Cloud CLI
Enter the following command:
gcloud storage buckets notifications create "gs://${METADATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --topic="${PUBSUB_TOPIC_NAME}" \ --event-types="OBJECT_FINALIZE" \ --payload-format="json" \ --project="${PROJECT_ID}"
f. Assign IAM permissions to the Zscaler service account.
Grant the Zscaler service account the necessary permissions to read from the buckets and manage Pub/Sub subscriptions.
Using Google Cloud Console
i. Grant bucket access.
In the Google Cloud console, go to Cloud Storage > Buckets. The Buckets page appears, listing all the buckets.
Grant bucket access to both the <PREFIX>-data bucket and the <PREFIX>-metadata bucket:
On the Buckets page, click the bucket name. The Bucket details page appears.
On the Bucket details page, click the Permissions tab.
Click Grant access. The Grant access page appears.
See image.
On the Grant access page, in the Add principals section, enter the Zscaler service account in the New principals field—for example, zscaler-sa-<PREFIX>@<PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
In the Assign roles section, from the Role drop-down menu, select the following roles:
Storage Object Viewer: Grants access to view objects and their metadata, excluding Access Control Lists (ACLs). It can also list the objects in a bucket.

Storage Legacy Bucket Reader: Grants permission to list a bucket's contents and read bucket metadata, excluding Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies. It also grants permission to read object metadata.
You must select both of these roles for each bucket.
See image.
Click Save.
ii. Grant Pub/Sub subscription management access.
In the Google Cloud console, go to IAM & Admin > IAM. The IAM page appears.
On the IAM page, click Grant access. The Grant access page appears.
See image.
On the Grant access page, in the Add principals section, enter the Zscaler service account in the New principals field—for example, zscaler-sa-<PREFIX>@<PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
In the Assign roles section, from the Role drop-down menu, select Pub/Sub Editor. This role can modify topics and subscriptions, and publish and consume messages.
See image.
Click Save.
iii. Grant the service account user role access to the Zscaler service account.
In the Google Cloud console, go to IAM & Admin > Service Accounts. The Service accounts page appears.
On the Service accounts page, click the Zscaler service account name in the list of service accounts—for example, zscaler-sa-<PREFIX>@<PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
See image.
On the service account details page, click the Principals with access tab and then click the View by principals subtab.
Click Grant access. The Grant access page appears.
See image.
On the Grant access page, in the Add principals section, enter the Zscaler service account in the New principals field—for example, zscaler-sa-<PREFIX>@<PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
In the Assign roles section, from the Role drop-down menu, select Service Account User. This role runs operations as the service account.
See image.
Click Save.
Using Google Cloud CLI
Enter the following commands to grant the Zscaler service account the necessary permissions to read from the buckets and manage Pub/Sub subscriptions:

# Grant Object Viewer role on the data bucket gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding "gs://${DATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --member="serviceAccount:${ZSCALER_SA}" \ --role="roles/storage.objectViewer" # Grant Legacy Bucket Reader role on the data bucket gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding "gs://${DATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --member="serviceAccount:${ZSCALER_SA}" \ --role="roles/storage.legacyBucketReader" # Grant Object Viewer role on the metadata bucket gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding "gs://${METADATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --member="serviceAccount:${ZSCALER_SA}" \ --role="roles/storage.objectViewer" # Grant Legacy Bucket Reader role on the metadata bucket gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding "gs://${METADATA_BUCKET_NAME}" \ --member="serviceAccount:${ZSCALER_SA}" \ --role="roles/storage.legacyBucketReader" # Grant Pub/Sub Editor role on the project gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding "${PROJECT_ID}" \ --member="serviceAccount:${ZSCALER_SA}" \ --role="roles/pubsub.editor" # Grant Service Account User role to impersonate the service account itself. Necessary to generate its own credentials gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding serviceAccount:${ZSCALER_SA} \ --member="serviceAccount:${ZSCALER_SA}" \ --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountUser"
g. Create the service account private key.
To create a private key:
In the Google Cloud console, go to IAM & Admin > Service Accounts. The Service accounts page appears.
On the Service accounts page, filter to find the newly created service account and select it. The service account details page appears.
See image.
On the service account details page, click the Keys tab.
On the Keys tab, from the Add key drop-down menu, select Create new key. The Create private key window appears.
See image.
In the Create private key window, select JSON as the Key type and click Create.
See image.

A file containing the service account key values is downloaded to your local system. These values are required when creating the DLP GCP Integration in the Zscaler Admin Console. The following image displays example key values.
See image.
2. Add a DLP GCP application integration in Workflow Automation.
To add a DLP GCP application integration using the GCP service account private key:

From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Workflow Automation > Integrations. The Integrations dashboard appears, displaying a DLP GCP application tile. The Tile View icon is selected by default.
See image.
(Optional) On the Integrations dashboard, change the view format for the dashboard. Click the List View icon to view the DLP GCP application in a list.
See image.
After you select a view option, perform one of the following procedures:
In the tile view:
In the DLP GCP application tile, click the Add icon. The add Zscaler DLP GCP Integration page appears.
In the list view:
Click Connect next to the DLP GCP application integration. The Zscaler DLP GCP Integration details page appears, displaying a Configuration Steps tab and a Configuration tab.
On the Configuration tab, click Add New. The add Zscaler DLP GCP Integration page appears.
See image.
On the add Zscaler DLP GCP Integration page, in the Zscaler GCP DLP Integration section:
Integration Name: Enter a name for the integration.
Project ID: From the JSON key downloaded from the Google Cloud console, copy the project_id for the DLP integration and enter it here.
Private Key: From the JSON key downloaded from the Google Cloud console, copy the private_key for the DLP integration and enter it here.
Client Email: From the JSON key downloaded from the Google Cloud console, copy the client_email for the DLP integration and enter it here.
Prefix for Bucket and Topic: Enter a prefix for the storage bucket and topic.
In the Privacy Settings section:

Hide Evidence Data - Admin: Select if you do not want admins to be able to generate presigned evidence links for an incident on the Violation Content tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can generate evidence links. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Trigger Data - Admin: Select if you do not want admins to be able to see the trigger data for an incident on the Violation Content tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can see the trigger data. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details - Admin: Select if you do not want the admins to be able to view any of the policy details for the incident on the Violation Details tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can view the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is not selected by default.

Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - Admin: Select if you do not want the admins to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident on the Violation Details tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can view these sections of the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - Admin checkbox. This checkbox is not selected by default.

Hide Evidence Data - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to generate presigned evidence links for an incident. Otherwise, they can generate evidence links. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Trigger Data - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to see the trigger data for an incident. Otherwise, they can see the trigger data. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to view any of the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view these sections of the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - End User checkbox.

Hide Evidence Data - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to generate presigned evidence links for the incident. Otherwise, they can generate evidence links. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Trigger Data - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to see the trigger data for the incident. Otherwise, they can see the trigger data. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to view the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view these sections of the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - Manager/Approver checkbox.
See image.

If you disable Hide Evidence Data or Hide Trigger Data in the integration, but you did not enable read access to the storage accounts when creating the cloud resources, no one can generate evidence links or view trigger data in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Click Validate. The system validates the account credentials that are entered with the GCP integration. You can only add the integration if it passes validation.

If the validation fails for any reason, or if the configuration has been created or updated with the wrong values, you must disable and re-enable the integration after you correct the values for the integration.
Click Add. The Zscaler DLP GCP Integration details page appears, displaying the DLP integration under Connected Accounts with an Enabled status.
To learn more, see Managing DLP GCP Application Integrations in Workflow Automation.
After you add the DLP GCP application integration in Zscaler Admin Console, you can verify whether the DLP application integration was successful in the Google Cloud console.
To view the integration:
Log in to the Google Admin Console.
Using the Project Selection drop-down menu, select your organization.
From the resource table that appears, select the appropriate domain.
Using the Search bar, search for Subscriptions and select it. The Subscription page appears.
On the Subscription page, filter the DLP integration by name or prefix you provided in the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
You can view the DLP GCP integration you added in the Zscaler Admin Console.
3. Set Up the DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding.

Configure the DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding on a GCP instance for Workflow Automation. To learn more about configuring Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding in GCP, see Configuring DLP Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding for Google Cloud.

blocks.text: After you configure the DLP application integration, the DLP incidents that occur in your organization are displayed on the Incidents page in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see Managing Incidents.
